statement: South Korea's semiconductor exports rose 262.8 percent year on year to 60.30 billion dollars in September 2026, passing 60 billion dollars in a single month for the first time, which the report ties to expanding AI infrastructure investment and resulting memory-chip price increases.
why: South Korea is the main source of high-bandwidth memory used in AI accelerators, so a record single month of chip exports shows memory output and shipments running at full stretch while prices climb.

impact.mechanism: Record memory shipments feed accelerator assembly and so ease one supply bottleneck, but the accompanying memory price increases raise the component cost inside every accelerator and server built from them.

evidence.source: Xinhua (English edition, wire restatement citing South Korean trade data)
evidence.excerpt: skyrocketed 262.8 percent to 60.30 billion dollars, crossing 60 billion dollars for the first time

evidence.source: Xinhua (English edition, wire restatement citing South Korean trade data)
evidence.excerpt: the continuous expansion of AI infrastructure investments that led to price hikes in memory chips
